propers.name: Secret
propers.text:
Concede nobis, quaesumus, Domine, haec digne frequentare mysteria: quia,
quoties hujus hostiae commemoratio celebratur, opus nostrae redemptionis
exercetur. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, Filium tuum: Qui tecum vivit
et regnat in unitate.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1862 sets no comma after quaesumus; 1962 has 'quaesumus, Domine,'; 1862 conclusion is the short cue 'Per Dominum.'; 1962 prints 'Per Dominum nostrum.'; A GAP, RECORDED NOT REPAIRED: the opening word is destroyed by the ornamental initial. Line 49433 reads 'ri nobis, qusesumus D6-'. The printed word is a drop-cap T followed by 'ui'; the layer gives only 'ri'. No public-domain witness read here recovers those letters directly.. Corroboration: Venice 1570 at text-layer lines 50470-50474 prints this Postcommunion in its own Dominica IX formulary and its body agrees word for word ('... nobis, quesumus domine, communio sacramenti, purificationem conferat, et tribuat vnitatem. Per do.'), but its own OCR of the opening word is likewise wrecked ('F1 8i'). Vatican typica 1604 has the same prayer at the same place (around line 37995) and its OCR of the whole line is unusable. So the prayer is corroborated in two further public-domain witnesses and the initial letters are not.. Recorded limitation: The strongest thing that can be said for 'Tui' is internal: this scan renders the drop-cap T of 'Tua nos' (Seventh Sunday Postcommunion, line 49093) as 'rp', so 'r' standing for a drop-cap T is behaviour this file demonstrates elsewhere in the same lane; and no other prayer begins '_ _ _ nobis, quaesumus Domine, communio sacramenti'. That is inference, not reading, which is why this is medium and why the antecedent text above keeps the brackets. WHAT I COULD NOT DO: read the 1862 page image. The 1862's whole-document page images and facsimile PDF are registered `storage = remote`, the brief forbids downloading, and the eight tracked BookReader leaves (221, 303, 347-349, 700-706, 721-725) do not include this page — leaf = printed folio + 85, so printed p. 331 would be leaf 416. Target text is given in the project's calendar rendering: unaccented, ae/oe expanded to two letters, printed line wraps joined, and the typica's i normalised to the project's j where it occurs. The typica itself prints no j in this prayer. That normalisation is the project's standing practice (src/sources/calendars/roman-1962/propers.yaml records it in terms at lines 20439, 43595 and 43622).
